We need prefix[j+1] - prefix[i] == (j+1) - i, i.e., prefix[j+1] - (j+1) == prefix[i] - i. So we define f(k) = prefix[k] - k. We count pairs (i, j+1) where i < j+1 and f(i) == f(j+1).     prefix = 0
    freq[0] = 1
    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        prefix += int(s[k - 1])
        f = prefix - k
        count += freq[f]
        freq[f] += 1
    return count

We need prefix[j+1] - prefix[i] == (j+1) - i, i.e., prefix[j+1] - (j+1) == prefix[i] - i. So we define f(k) = prefix[k] - k. We count pairs (i, j+1) where i < j+1 and f(i) == f(j+1).     freq[0] = 1
    for k in range(1, n + 1):

        f = prefix - k
        count += freq[f]
        freq[f] += 1
    return count

An optimization: use prefix sums. Let prefix[i] = sum of digits of s[0..i-1]. For a substring s[i..j], sum of digits = prefix[j+1] - prefix[i], and length = j+1 - i. We need prefix[j+1] - prefix[i] == (j+1) - i, i.e., prefix[j+1] - (j+1) == prefix[i] - i. So we define f(k) = prefix[k] - k. We count pairs (i, j+1) where i < j+1 and f(i) == f(j+1). def count_Substrings(s):
    n = len(s)
    count = 0
    freq = defaultdict(int)
    # f(0) = prefix[0] - 0 = 0
    prefix = 0
    freq[0] = 1
    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        prefix += int(s[k - 1])
        f = prefix - k
        count += freq[f]
        freq[f] += 1
    return count
